headline: Kai, September's 29,000 payrolls all but killed an October hike, and the G7 is opening the taps against $100 crude.
subline: Hike odds collapsed to 16%, Hormuz stayed shut with oil near $100, and Anthropic set course for the largest IPO ever.
asof: Weekend edition · strip shows Friday's close, October 2 · every figure links to its source below

items.title: September payrolls land at 29,000
items.sentence: The U.S. added 29,000 jobs in September against 90,000 expected, and unemployment ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: An October hike is all but off
items.sentence: Bond traders cut the odds of an October rate increase to 16% from 64% a week earlier, and all three major indexes closed Friday higher on the news, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: G7 opens reserves against record diesel
items.sentence: The G7 and the IEA will release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude over four months, a large share within 20 days, to pull fuel prices off record highs, per UPI.

items.title: Nvidia tops $5.7 trillion intraday
items.sentence: Nvidia traded as high as $237.88 on Friday, pushing its market value past $5.7 trillion, per TheStreet.

items.title: Quiet data week, then earnings season
items.sentence: Monday brings September ISM services, Wednesday the Fed's September minutes, and Thursday PepsiCo's results, a light slate before earnings season gathers pace the following week, per CMC Markets.

items.title: Hormuz stays shut as ceasefire talks stall
items.sentence: Tehran awaits a formal U.S. answer on a seven-day ceasefire and phased Hormuz reopening that Trump has publicly dismissed, with the closed strait still disrupting roughly 20% of the world's traded oil and gas, per CBS News.

items.title: Third carrier group ordered to the region
items.sentence: The Pentagon is sending a third carrier strike group and 9,000 to 10,000 additional troops to the Middle East by the end of November, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: Supertanker burns in the Strait of Hormuz
items.sentence: A supertanker was struck and caught fire near Oman while transiting the strait, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: Shutdown averted ahead of the midterms
items.sentence: Senate leaders reached a funding deal that keeps the government open into the fall campaign season, per NBC News.

items.title: Ethiopia expels Eritrean diplomats
items.sentence: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Eritrea and expelled 10 diplomats over what it called direct and indirect acts of hostility, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: Anthropic points at a $2 trillion IPO
items.sentence: Anthropic is reportedly preparing to go public as soon as mid-November at up to a $2 trillion valuation, the largest IPO ever, after 2025 revenue of roughly $4.6 billion, per Yahoo Finance citing Bloomberg and Reuters.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon to defenders first
items.sentence: Google's new frontier model posts 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1 with a 1-million-token output limit and reaches trusted cyber defenders first under the Fairwind Program, per Google.

items.title: Six labs sign the superintelligence accord
items.sentence: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI and Nvidia signed the White House's one-page, 'morally binding' accord on four layers of controls and auditing, which Dario Amodei called 'a start,' per Axios.

items.title: OpenAI shelves GPT-6.1 Astra
items.sentence: OpenAI scrapped its planned GPT-6.1 Astra release after internal testing surfaced alignment failures, per AI Magazine.

items.title: Bitcoin reclaims $86,000 as Uptober opens
items.sentence: Bitcoin jumped over 2.2% to retake $86,000 on October 1, spot ETFs took in $102.7 million, and Citi raised its 12-month target to $113,000 from $82,000, per Coinpedia.
